theorem_title: Integer quartic comparison is exactly the analytic threshold test
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.cleared_switch_equivalence (J s j q : ℕ) (hJ : 0 < J) (hs : 0 < s) (hj : j < J) :
    clearedSwitch J s j q ↔
      threshold ((j : ℝ) / J) ≤ phi ((q : ℝ) / ((J - j) * s))  := by sorry
natural_language_statement: For arbitrary natural J,s,j,q with J>0, s>0 and j<J, the published clearedSwitch integer comparison holds if and only if P(q/((J-j)s)) is at least (v+j/J)/(1-j/J), with v=159243801/500000000 and the exact quartic P. There is no restriction on q beyond being a natural number. The positive-depth hypothesis identifies real subtraction with truncated natural subtraction and makes all cleared denominators positive.
